properties.value: SHA-1 ships in the build via the sha1 crate (transitive dependency — likely the WebSocket handshake digest consumer); available in the shipped library, no call site found in the application. Not directly changeable from this tree without identifying and replacing the dependent crate; the migration (SHA-384) applies only if a consumer ever calls it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 27 sites are == / != comparisons of PUBLIC digests (block, transaction, asset and genesis hashes) used for data-structure equality (PartialEq impls), DAG traversal, mempool ordering and wallet-sync checks. Neither operand is secret at any site, so the timing-leak premise of the mac-non-constant-time rule does not apply — this codebase performs no MAC/tag verification at all. Five sites (xelis_common/src/contract/tests/asset.rs:25,301,322,344 + one more) are test assertions. Kept as recorded

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.17.14 is pulled into the graph via rustls-webpki (part of the rustls 0.23.43 stack used by tokio-tungstenite for the miner's WebSocket). It ships X25519 key agreement and other primitives in the build; no first-party code calls ring directly, and rustls 0.23.43 uses the aws-lc-rs provider — observable here, replaceable by upgrading the rustls/rustls-webpki dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.17.14 is in the dependency tree (transitive, via rustls for the wallet's HTTP stack), so its Ed25519 implementation ships in the binary; verified there are no ring:: or ed25519 references anywhere in the workspace source — available in the shipped library, no application call site found. The network's real signature scheme is the first-party ElGamal/Schnorr scheme over Ristretto255 (reported as a separate finding), not ring's Ed25519.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Core of the XELIS confidential-transaction stack: the xelis-project FORK of curve25519-dalek (tag v5.0.2, built with the custom ecdlp feature — precomputed ECDLP tables let PrivateKey::decrypt recover u64 amounts, xelis_common/src/crypto/elgamal/key.rs:187-189). Ristretto255 group ops back the Twisted ElGamal homomorphic PKE, Pedersen commitments, the homegrown Schnorr signature, and the Bulletproofs range proofs. Consensus-critical: changeable only via a network hard fork, not by this repo alon

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS 1.3 capability via rustls 0.23.43, engaged when the miner/wallet WebSocket clients connect over wss://; no explicit cipher-suite or group configuration exists in first-party code, so the key exchange is whatever rustls negotiates by default (recent rustls + aws-lc-rs offer X25519MLKEM768 hybrid on TLS 1.3; classical X25519 otherwise). TLS 1.3 suites themselves encode no key exchange. Changeable here only via the rustls dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider ring 0.17.14 (BoringSSL-derived) in the dependency tree via rustls (transitive, for the wallet's HTTP server stack). No direct ring:: call sites in application code. Presence recorded per the provider-inventory rule.
